Subject: High-touch guarantee request + onboarding timeline

Mina — thanks again for the demo last week. ZenithEdge is close to a decision but our Security and Ops teams need a written availability guarantee (we're asking for a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment and a P95 latency target under 120ms for inference calls) for the first 12 months as part of the negotiated SOW.

Before we proceed to legal: a) can Redwood commit to those numbers for a single dedicated pool, and b) what product/engineering changes would be required for the go-live (we have bursty traffic and a hard launch on Sep 1).

Attached is the latest SOW draft (v2) and a small sample of their load profile. Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Best,

Thanks Oliver — bringing the right folks in. Short answers up front: we can offer a bespoke guarantee for a Dedicated pool, but it will require operational commitments, a small engineering checklist, and legal sign-off on scope/credit terms.

To make progress we need:
- Confirmation of expected sustained RPS and burst profile for first 30/90 days (fine-grained than the CSV sample).
- Agreement to a capacity reservation (Dedicated pool) and an initial warm-up window before launch.
- Scope boundaries (which endpoints, max request size, and whether streaming is in scope for the SLA).

Marcus, Dev — can you review the attached perf CSV and call out blockers for the 99.95% / P95 <120ms ask assuming a single Dedicated GPU pool in us-west? Also note we may need a short-term fallback policy (auto-failover to hosted variants) for the first two weeks of launch.

Oliver — happy to schedule a 30m call tomorrow if that helps. If legal needs a redlineable clause, please flag which customer-facing language they expect.

Thanks,
Mina

Subject: Re: High-touch guarantee request + onboarding timeline

Quick read of the CSV + ask. TL;DR: technically feasible with constraints. Details and action items below.

Observations:
- The sample shows 800 RPS sustained with spikes to ~3k for short windows. If ZenithEdge buys a Dedicated pool sized for sustained 1k RPS with a 3k burst buffer we can meet P95 <120ms in most cases.
- Cold-cache/initialization on new model variants is the primary risk for early launches — KV cache priming and staged warm-up are required.
- Multi-region failover will add complexity; for now assume single-region (us-west) is acceptable to the customer.

Engineering asks (for roadmap/ops):
1) Reserve a Dedicated pool: estimate 4x A100-equiv GPUs (Dev, can you confirm exact instance sizing?).
2) Short-term: enable aggressive prefix KV cache and pre-warm for top 50 prompts (we'll need sample prompt list).
3) Ops: define an escalation playbook if P95 breaches for more than 15 minutes (alerting + automatic alert thresholds).

Risks to surface to Sales/Legal:
- SLA credits: we need a cap for credits tied to observable platform outages only (not customer-side misconfig).
- Feature gates: streaming sessions at >2x median tokens/sec could require a separate operational SLA.

I attached a quick perf summary and the run-output for the CSV sample.

Marcus
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: perf_summary_for_zenithedge.pdf (application/pdf), 112KB]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High-touch guarantee request + onboarding timeline

Thanks — a couple of roadmap notes and a proposal for reduced risk:

- Roadmap: the new batching optimization for v1.9 (landing Aug) will materially reduce p95 by ~15-25% for the typical prompt length. We can prioritize that backport to the Dedicated serving infra as a paid accel.
- Proposal: offer a staged SLA ramp. Example: Month 0–1 (pilot): 99.9% / P95 <150ms with active debugging; Month 2–12: 99.95% / P95 <120ms once we complete cache priming and the v1.9 backport. That reduces exposure while giving the customer roadmap visibility.

Operations note: we need a signed SOW with a 2-week warm-up window where the customer agrees to traffic shaping to allow cache priming. If legal wants explicit exclusion language for synthetic load/pen tests, include that.

Dev
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

1) ZenithEdge to confirm expected RPS and burst windows in more detail (ideally per-endpoint CSV).
2) Legal: expect a redline of the SLA clause from Lauren by 2027-07-15 17:00 PT.
3) Engineering: Dev to scope the v1.9 backport timeline and confirm exact infra sizing (Dev to confirm by 2027-07-16).
4) Operations: define the runbook and alert thresholds; Marcus will share draft incident taxonomy.

If that plan works, I'll mark the account as "high-touch onboarding" and push the SOW to procurement. If you prefer a call, I'm available 2–3pm PT today.

Best,
